summary: Frontend retest at 375x667. Auth login with padre.test@timeguard.dev / Familia123 works and Supabase session persists. Dashboard STILL renders the 'Falta preparar Supabase' error panel (variant: 'No pudimos cargar los dispositivos. Revisa las políticas RLS.') because supabase.from('devices').select('id,name,profile_name,online,blocked,platform,pairing_code')... returns HTTP 400 PGRST 42703 'column devices.name does not exist'. Same drift on extra_time_requests.minutes. All 11 tables now exist, but the `devices` and `extra_time_requests` tables were created by an earlier partial migration WITHOUT the columns declared in /app/supabase/schema.sql. Because the schema uses `create table if not exists`, re-running it does NOT add the missing columns. Every downstream flow (tabs beyond error panel, pairing, block toggle, simulate-request, approve/deny, persistence after reload, sign-out from Ajustes) is blocked by this schema drift and could not be exercised end-to-end.

critical.issue: HTTP 400 - code 42703: columns devices.name, devices.profile_name, devices.online, devices.blocked, devices.platform DO NOT EXIST. Only id, family_id, pairing_code, created_at, last_seen_at are present. This is the exact call load() makes after resolving family_members, so the dashboard bricks immediately for every logged-in parent.
HTTP 400 - code 42703: column extra_time_requests.minutes does not exist. Blocks the entire 'solicitudes de tiempo extra' feature that is the primary focus of this iteration.

integration_issues.issue: devices SELECT fails with 400/42703 (missing columns), so load() sets loadError and shows the 'Falta preparar Supabase' panel. Nothing beyond auth can be tested.
Even if devices were fixed, inserting/reading extra_time_requests would fail because the 'minutes' column is missing; createRequest and load() both use it.

action_items: Alternative: DROP TABLE devices, extra_time_requests CASCADE and re-run /app/supabase/schema.sql (will also drop any test rows).

After fix, verify with:
curl -H "apikey: $ANON" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" '<url>/rest/v1/devices?select=id,name,profile_name,online,blocked,platform,pairing_code&limit=1' -> HTTP 200.

Consider making /app/supabase/schema.sql self-healing: after each `create table if not exists`, add matching `alter table ... add column if not exists ...` for every declared column, so re-running the file always converges.

Optional (already noted in iteration_3): surface memberError.details / raw supabase error text in the loadError panel instead of just 'Revisa las políticas RLS' — the current generic message hid a schema-column error for two iterations.
critical_code_review_comments: The 'schema drift' failure mode (table exists but columns missing) is invisible from the app's error UI, which blames RLS. Show the underlying Supabase error message in the error panel to shorten future debugging.

In index.tsx load(), if the auto-create-family branch runs and `families.insert(...).select().single()` fails (e.g. RLS), member stays undefined and busy is set to false without setting loadError, leaving the user on a blank screen. Add explicit error handling for that INSERT.
Realtime handler on line 68 already switched to silent load (load(true)), that part looks correct in this build.
index.tsx is a single ~91-line dense file mixing 7 components; still workable but splitting would help future testability (already noted in iteration_3).

success_rate.backend: Auth + tables reachable (11/11 exist), but 2/11 have missing columns; ~82% column coverage. Feature endpoints: devices SELECT 0%, extra_time_requests SELECT 0%.

rca_of_issue: Root cause: schema drift between /app/supabase/schema.sql and the live Supabase database. In iteration_3 several tables were missing; the user re-ran schema.sql to fix that, and now ALL 11 tables answer 200. BUT the older partial migration had already created public.devices and public.extra_time_requests with a reduced column set. Because schema.sql uses `create table if not exists`, the DDL for those two tables was skipped on the re-run and the missing columns (devices.name, profile_name, online, blocked, platform; extra_time_requests.minutes) were never added. load() in /app/frontend/app/index.tsx line 61 then issues SELECT id,name,profile_name,online,blocked,platform,pairing_code on devices, PostgREST returns 400 42703, d.error is truthy, loadError is set and the 'Falta preparar Supabase' panel is rendered — hiding every UI flow beyond auth. Mitigation: run the ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS statements listed under action_items and NOTIFY pgrst 'reload schema'. Long-term: make schema.sql idempotent at column level, not just table level.
